Background to the PSR

content_blocks.text: The government’s aim was for the “ PSR to move away from the expectation of tendering for healthcare services in all circumstances and towards collaboration across the health and care system. This is intended to remove unnecessary tendering, remove barriers to integrating care and promote the development of stable collaborations. ”
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
Background to the PSR

content_blocks.text: Additionally, the aim of PSR is to make it “ straightforward to continue with existing arrangements for service provision where those arrangements are working well and there is no value for the patients, taxpayers and population in seeking an alternative provider. ”
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
Background to the PSR

content_blocks.text: The PSR has five routes to contract for decision-makers to consider.
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
Background to the PSR

content_blocks.text: Whichever route commissioners opt for, there are several key criteria which decision-making bodies will be bound to consider when deciding who to arrange services with. Broadly, these criteria are:
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
Background to the PSR

content_blocks.text: Quality (safety, effectiveness and experience) and innovation
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
Background to the PSR

content_blocks.text: Value
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
Background to the PSR

content_blocks.text: Integration, collaboration and service sustainability
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
Background to the PSR

content_blocks.text: Access, reducing inequalities and choice
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
Background to the PSR

content_blocks.text: Social value
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
Background to the PSR

content_blocks.text: Below we have set out the five routes to awarding contracts under the PSR.

content_blocks.text: Direct Award A
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A

content_blocks.text: Direct Award A is used in the circumstances that the services can only be provided by the existing
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A

content_blocks.text: provider and there is no realistic alternative. This is detailed more thoroughly in Regulation 7 .
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A

content_blocks.text: To use Direct Award A, the service must be an existing service provided by an existing provider, the Authority must be satisfied that those services can only be provided by that provider, and the service must not be a framework.
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A

content_blocks.text: The types of services covered by Direct Award A are likely to be essential services provided by NHS Trusts under the Standard Contract, such as 999 emergency ambulance services and NHS urgent mental health crisis services.
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A

content_blocks.text: To award a contract under Direct Award A, the Authority must publish notice of the award within 30 days of the award (that is, the signing of the contract). The requirements of a valid notice are set out in Schedule 2.
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A

content_blocks.text: Direct Award B
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Direct Award B

content_blocks.text: Direct Award B is used where the patient has a choice of provider and there is no restriction on
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Direct Award B

content_blocks.text: provider numbers. Direct Award B must be used if the following circumstances apply:
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Direct Award B

content_blocks.text: (i) the health care services are ones where patients get a choice of provider (either because the relevant Authority has decided to offer patients a choice or because there is a legal obligation to offer choice);
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Direct Award B

content_blocks.text: (ii) there is no restriction on the number of providers;
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Direct Award B

content_blocks.text: (iii) contracts are offered to all providers who meet all requirements for delivering the services in question;
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Direct Award B

content_blocks.text: (iv) steps have been taken to make providers aware of these contracts and of how to express an interest; and
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Direct Award B

content_blocks.text: (v) it is not a framework.
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Direct Award B

content_blocks.text: The award process is the same as that for Direct Award A, above.
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Direct Award B

content_blocks.text: Direct Award C
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Direct Award C

content_blocks.text: Direct Award C is used where the Authority intends to continue working with an existing provider.
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Direct Award C

content_blocks.text: The conditions for Direct Award C are:
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Direct Award C

content_blocks.text: (i) the Authority is not obliged to use either Direct Award A or B;
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Direct Award C

content_blocks.text: (ii) there is an existing contract which is about to expire, and a subsequent contract must replace it;
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Direct Award C

content_blocks.text: (iii) the considerable change threshold is not met; this test will be met where:
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Direct Award C

content_blocks.text: a. new arrangements significantly change the nature of the contract from when it was first entered into;
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Direct Award C

content_blocks.text: b. if there are no material changes to the contract, the lifetime value of contract is considered – if it is at least either:
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Direct Award C

content_blocks.text: i. £500k higher; and
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Direct Award C

content_blocks.text: ii. 25% higher,
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Direct Award C

content_blocks.text: then Direct Award C route is not available, and the Authority must use either the Most Suitable Provider or Competitive Process. It is worth noting that some exclusions do however apply, which are detailed at Regulation 6;
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Direct Award C

content_blocks.text: (iv) The Authority believes, taking in account the Key Criteria and applying the Basic Selection Criteria (see below for these) that the incumbent is satisfying the requirements of the existing contract and this will continue under the new contract; and
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Direct Award C

content_blocks.text: (v) it is not a framework agreement.
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Direct Award C

content_blocks.text: To award a contract under Direct Award C, the Authority must publish a notice of intention to
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Direct Award C

content_blocks.text: award as well as the confirmation of award required in Direct Award processes A and B.
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Direct Award C

content_blocks.text: The Key Criteria are set out at Regulation 5 (and detailed at Annex D of the Statutory Guidance):
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Direct Award C

content_blocks.text: (i) quality and innovation;
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Direct Award C

content_blocks.text: (ii) value;
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Direct Award C

content_blocks.text: (iii) integration, collaboration and service sustainability;
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Direct Award C

content_blocks.text: (iv) improving access, reducing health inequalities and facilitating choice; and
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Direct Award C

content_blocks.text: (v) social value.
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Direct Award C

content_blocks.text: The Authority should record in the decision-making record for the relevant process the reasons
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Direct Award C

content_blocks.text: why it favours some of the criteria above over others. It must ensure it continues to comply with its
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Direct Award C

content_blocks.text: obligations under existing legislation and statutory and NHS guidance outside of the PSR.
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Direct Award C

content_blocks.text: The Basic Selection Criteria are not prescribed but must be decided by the Authority, they may
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Direct Award C

content_blocks.text: relate to the selection criteria under the PCR 2015, i.e.:
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Direct Award C

content_blocks.text: (i) suitability to carry out a specific activity (obviously one which is in relation to the contract)
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Direct Award C

content_blocks.text: (ii) economic and financial standing, and
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Direct Award C

content_blocks.text: (iii) technical and professional ability,
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Direct Award C

content_blocks.text: (see Regulation 19 and Schedule 16 for more detail)

Direct Award A
Direct Award C

content_blocks.text: Most Suitable Provider
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Most Suitable Provider

content_blocks.text: The Most Suitable Provider route may be used where an Authority believes it can identify the
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Most Suitable Provider

content_blocks.text: most suitable provider, taking into account the ‘likely providers’ and all information available at the
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Most Suitable Provider

content_blocks.text: time.
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Most Suitable Provider

content_blocks.text: It may be followed provided there is no obligation to use Direct Award A or B and the conditions
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Most Suitable Provider

content_blocks.text: allowing use of Direct Award C are either not met or they are met but the Most Suitable Provider
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Most Suitable Provider

content_blocks.text: route is preferable to the Authority.
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Most Suitable Provider

content_blocks.text: The guidance urges Authorities to carry out ‘pre-market engagement’ to ensure more efficient
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Most Suitable Provider

content_blocks.text: outcomes.
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Most Suitable Provider

content_blocks.text: To award a contract under Most Suitable Provider, the Authority must:
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Most Suitable Provider

content_blocks.text: (i) notify providers of its intention to use this process. Schedule 5 does not stipulate that authorities must expressly invite providers to get in touch or how to do so but if they do, providers need to be taken into consideration by the Authority;
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Most Suitable Provider

content_blocks.text: (ii) wait 14 days after the notice is published, within which providers may respond to the notice. The Authority is not permitted to take any steps towards identifying potential providers until 14 days after the day on which it published the relevant notice, however this is not a standstill period;
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Most Suitable Provider

content_blocks.text: (iii) take into account any provider that responded to the notice about the intention to follow this process;
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Most Suitable Provider

content_blocks.text: (iv) identify potential providers with reference to the key criteria and basic selection criteria;and identify the most suitable provider and publish notice of its intention to award. Subject to no representations being made by unsuccessful providers, the contract can be awarded at the end of the standstill period.
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Most Suitable Provider

content_blocks.text: The necessary notices for the Most Suitable Provider process are:
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Most Suitable Provider

content_blocks.text: (i) intention to use the MSP process
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Most Suitable Provider

content_blocks.text: (ii) intention to award; and
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Most Suitable Provider

content_blocks.text: (iii) confirmation of award.
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
Most Suitable Provider

content_blocks.text: The Competitive Process
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
The Competitive Process

content_blocks.text: The Competitive Process may be used where the other processes do not apply.
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
The Competitive Process

content_blocks.text: To award a contract under the Competitive Process, the Authority must:
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
The Competitive Process

content_blocks.text: (i) decide on the award criteria;
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
The Competitive Process

content_blocks.text: (ii) consider the Key Criteria and the Basic Selection Criteria (as above)
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
The Competitive Process

content_blocks.text: (iii) publish a notice seeking offers (the requirements of this notice are in Schedule 8 ). The competition may be broken down into stages but the Authority must state this in its Schedule 8 notice. The stages are not prescribed; it is possible for commissioners to use, for example, the restricted procedure under the PCR 2015; and
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
The Competitive Process

content_blocks.text: (iv) assess offers and notify the winning provider of its success. Unsuccessful providers must be given the information set out in Schedule 9 , such as the reasons why the successful provider won and the reasons why the unsuccessful provider did not. ‘Relative advantages and characteristics’ need not be considered as under the PCR 2015.
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
The Competitive Process

content_blocks.text: Notices are important to the collaborative process as they improve transparency. Transparency notices are to be published on the government’s Find a Tender website. We expect notice templates are to be developed but for the time being, an Authority will need to adapt the notices which are already available.
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
The Competitive Process

content_blocks.text: The necessary notices are:
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
The Competitive Process

content_blocks.text: (i) a notice of intention to award – this triggers the standstill period (see below); and
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
Direct Award A
The Competitive Process

content_blocks.text: (ii) confirmation of award.
heading_path: The five routes to awarding contracts under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR)
The Five Routes to Awarding Contracts
